summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, malnutrition, and congenital long QT syndrome, was admitted for abdominal pain and acute-on-chronic diarrhea. He reported symptoms similar to prior C. difficile infection. CT scan showed no obstruction or colitis, but stool testing confirmed C. difficile with positive PCR and toxin. Oral vancomycin was started for a 14-day course. His G-tube was clogged on admission, leading to supplemental nutrition; it was successfully exchanged on hospital day 4. Creatinine rose to 2.4 due to poor oral intake but improved to baseline with IV fluids. Blood pressure remained elevated, prompting initiation of amlodipine. He was discharged home with services to continue tube feeds, complete antibiotics, and follow up with his primary team.
problems: Enterocolitis due to Clostridium difficile, not specified as recurrent
